newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end slightly lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end slightly lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed slightly lower on Monday in sluggish trade as foreign investors remained sidelined on expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates, Peruvian brokers said.
They forecast further falls for Tuesday on corrections after last week's gains and continuing low interest from abroad.
"The foreigners are waiting for the decision of the U.S. Federal Reserve, if interest rates go up or not," said Jose Guillen, of MGS y Asociados brokerage.
In Monday's session, the General Index .IGRA lost 0.30 percent to 1,566.67 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.21 percent to 2,087.78.
Total market volume was 32.05 million soles ($12.81 million) on 1,665 trades as overall 22 stocks rose, 34 fell and 32 were flat.

"Today's volume is not real, because there have been three important crosses which have increased volume," said Juan Carlos Palacios, of Helvetia brokerage. "In reality, we should close at around 15 million soles, which is very low."
After a three million share cross at 4.30 soles, bottler Embotelladora Latinoamericana was the biggest mover in the market, accounting for 40.98 percent of trade on 13.14 million soles of shares.
The bottler closed the session unchanged at 4.30 soles.

Brokers said investor attention concentrated on breweries among the leaders and on industrial stocks among the second- and third-tier shares. Benchmark Telefonica del Peru was the second most highly-traded stock, accounting for 14.74 percent of trade, as it too remained unchanged at 5.59 soles on 846,716 shares.
Brewery Compania Nacional Cervecera gained 5.88 percent to 1.26 soles on 1.75 million shares, while another brewery, Backus y Johnston, ended off 0.72 percent to 2.76 soles on 463,931 shares.

Leading mining stocks suffered, with Atacocha off 4.65 percent to 0.41 soles, Morococha dipping 2.48 percent to 1.57 soles, Minsur losing 0.34 percent to 23.7 soles and Southern Copper Corp off 1.37 percent to $14.45.
